map.输入制浆原料（木片、废纸等）重量与所得纸浆重量，计算纸浆得率（%）并评估制浆效率: Enter the weight of pulping raw material (chips, waste paper etc.) and the weight of pulp produced to compute the pulp yield (%) and assess pulping efficiency. Used for mill cost accounting and process optimization.
map.纸浆得率 = 纸浆重量 / 原料重量 × 100%: Pulp yield = pulp weight / raw material weight x 100%
map.根据原料重量与所得纸浆重量计算得率，评估制浆效率: Compute the yield from the raw material weight and the resulting pulp weight to assess pulping efficiency
map.制浆工艺评价中，由原料与成浆质量核算得率(%)，评估纤维利用率。: In pulp process evaluation, compute the yield (%) from the raw material and the pulp quality to assess fibre utilization.
map.成本分析中，得率直接影响吨浆原料消耗与能耗。: In cost analysis, yield directly affects raw material consumption and energy use per tonne of pulp.
map.工艺改进前后对比得率，量化蒸煮/磨浆优化效果。: Compare yield before and after process improvement to quantify the effect of cooking or grinding optimization.
map.算例：化学浆得率（原料 1000kg，纸浆 480kg）: Worked example: chemical pulp yield (raw material 1000kg, pulp 480kg)
map.：得率=480/1000×100=48.00%，属『化学浆』区间(40%–60%: Yield = 480/1000 x 100 = 48.00%, which falls in the "chemical pulp" band (40%-60%); pulp per tonne of raw material = 480/1000 = 0.4800 tonne. Formula: yield = pulp / raw material x 100%.
map.：≥85% 高得率（机械浆），60%–85% 半化学浆，40%–60% 化学浆，: >=85% high yield (mechanical pulp), 60%-85% semi-chemical pulp, 40%-60% chemical pulp, <40% low yield. The higher the yield the more fully the fibre is used, but strength is usually lower, so choose according to the product's positioning.
map.为什么机械浆得率高但强度低？: Why Does Mechanical Pulp Have High Yield but Low Strength?
map.机械浆保留几乎全部纤维故得率高，但木素未被大量去除，纤维间结合弱、易返黄；化学浆: Mechanical pulp retains nearly all the fibre so its yield is high, but lignin is not largely removed, so the fibre bonds are weak and it yellows easily; chemical pulp removes lignin and has a lower yield but better strength and durability. Choose between them by end use.
map.得率是关键因子：得率每升 1 个百分点，吨浆原料消耗同比例下降。但需结合能耗与化: Yield is the key factor: every percentage point of yield cuts raw material consumption per tonne of pulp by the same proportion. But it must be weighed against energy and chemical costs, because high-yield mechanical pulp often uses more electricity.
